name: Sign Rank / Star Number (Functional Upper Bound)
details: There is a finite-valued nondecreasing function f, independent of the class, with $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal H)\le f(\mathrm S(\mathcal H))$ for every finite binary class. An explicit choice is $f(d)=2F(d+2,d+2)^2$, with the chain-partition recurrence F spelled out in the survey. This is not an affine bound and is deliberately omitted from Hasse ranks and edges. Affine control in either direction is refuted by relationship sign_rank_star_number_incomparable.
proof_source: Survey prop:star-signrank-functional independently checks the matching-to-star shift and rank-two block assembly, importing Atminas's published Theorem 2.1. The same qualitative argument appears in Blondal et al. v2 Theorem 1.9; this is not blanket verification of that preprint.
witness_verification: For n>=4, the star number is n and sign rank is three. In this upper-bound orientation it is the second parameter that grows. This excludes any finite-valued reverse bound S<=g(SR), hence also any reverse affine bound.
